text: Conventions: plate comments in this file use the PROPOSED new names of globals (engine_retarder_*, fan_drive_*, all_speed_governor_*, j1939_engine_retarder_source_address ...), so apply the global renames and the function plate comments together. All 68 proposed names were checked for exact collisions against global_variables.csv / function_renames.csv / arrays.csv / constants.csv / enums.csv (0 collisions, 0 duplicates). Evidence base: decompiled C, xref_addr.py, disasm_func.py, the RAM dump (originals/cm848_ram.bin, base 0x3FA000), the ROM image (originals/cm848_rom.bin) and the j1939 MongoDB (PGN 61440 = ERC1, 65213 = FD1, 65249 = RC, 0 = TSC1; SPN 520 / 571 / 572 / 900 / 975 / 977 / 518 / 695 / 897).

plate_comment: Builds and sends the ECM's ERC1 broadcast (PGN 61440, source address j1939_engine_retarder_source_address, every 100 ms on retarder queue 1 so only while datalink_broadcast_enable_flags bit 3 is set, 2 data bytes). Byte 1 = retarder torque mode (SPN 900: 1 operator selection, 2 cruise control, 6 / 7 / 5 for TSC1 requester index 1 / 2 / 3 = transmission / ABS / ASR, 14 other, chosen from engine_retarder_request_source_code and engine_retarder_request_source_index) plus the brake assist switch bits (SPN 571, enabled while engine_retarder_selection_percent_fault_masked is non-zero), 0xFF when the retarder broadcast flag is clear. Byte 2 = actual retarder percent torque (SPN 520 = 125 minus engine_retarder_torque_percent_times_256 / 256 from cm848_calculateEngineRetarderTorque), 0xFF when the retarder broadcast flag is clear or engine_retarder_configuration_mode is 0 (was cm848_j1939BuildVehicleOperatingStatus).
evidence: Header 0xF000 + SA j1939_source_address_b are set by cm848_initJ1939SpeedControlMessage and the builder is queued with diag_record_queue_add_entry(1, 0xf000, 100, ...); j1939 DB PGN 61440 ERC1 = byte 1 SPN 900 mode (bits 1-4) + SPN 571 / 572 enable switches (bits 5-8), byte 2 SPN 520 actual retarder percent torque with offset -125 percent, and the code writes 0x7d - (percent x 256 >> 8) = 125 - percent. Mode nibble: request source code 3 -> 1 (operator selection), 2 -> 2 (cruise: governorOverrideSpeedControl), TSC1 requester index 1 / 2 / 3 -> 6 / 7 / 5 (ROM 0x5a470 TSC1 senders are SA 3 / 11 / 33 = transmission / brake controller / body controller), else 14. The lead (ERC1, not a vehicle operating status) holds.

plate_comment: Initialises the ERC1 transmit descriptor (PGN 61440 at 0x3fae10): CAN identifier from the priority word j1939_pgn61440_priority, 0xF000 and the engine retarder source address j1939_engine_retarder_source_address, data length 2 (j1939_pgn61440_tx_length), data pointer to the ERC1 byte 1 / byte 2 buffer at 0x3fae08; also resets the retarder torque lookup cache through cm848_initSpeedControlTableDimensions (was cm848_initJ1939SpeedControlMessage).
evidence: Writes header at 0x3fae10 (0xf00000 | priority << 26 | SA_b), length word +4, data pointer +6 = &j1939_vehicle_op_status_byte (0x3fae08), end pointer +10 = 0x3fae1e; it is the init partner of the ERC1 builder and is called from cm848_j1939_system_init beside the other PGN buffer inits. The three descriptor fields are mislabelled pgn65269 in the CSV (see the global rows).

plate_comment: Builds and sends the ECM's FD1 broadcast (PGN 65213, every 1000 ms on queue 0, 2 data bytes): byte 1 = engine fan 1 estimated percent speed (SPN 975, 0.4 percent per bit = fan_drive_estimated_speed_percent_times_256 x 5 >> 9, so 25600 gives 250 = 100 percent), byte 2 = fan drive state (SPN 977) in the low nibble with the reserved nibble set, 0xFE when fan_drive_state_code is above 15. Neither input is written anywhere in this firmware, so the frame always reports 0 percent and state 0 (fan off); the two parameters of the function are unused (was cm848_j1939SendDiagnosticStatusMessage).
evidence: Queue entry (0, 0xfebd, 1000, ...); j1939 DB PGN 65213 = Fan Drive #1 (FD1: SPN 975 engine fan 1 estimated percent speed, SPN 977 fan drive state). 25600 * 5 >> 9 = 250 = 100 percent at 0.4 percent per bit. xref_addr.py: j1939_diag_param_a (0x40a2a8) and j1939_diag_code (0x40a292) are read only in this function with 0 writes anywhere, and are 0 in the RAM dump. The lead (FD1, not a retarder or diagnostic status message) holds.

plate_comment: Initialises the FD1 transmit descriptor (PGN 65213 at 0x3fae28): CAN identifier from the priority word j1939_pgn65213_priority_cal, 0xFEBD and the engine source address j1939_source_address, data length 2 (word at 0x3fae2c), data pointer to the FD1 byte 1 / byte 2 buffer at 0x3fae20 and end pointer 0x3fae36 (was cm848_initJ1939BrakeRetarderBuffer).
evidence: Header = (priority & 7) << 2 : 0xfebd00 then the low byte set from j1939_source_address (the engine SA, not the retarder SA), length 2, data pointer &j1939_pgn65213_diag_param_byte; it only prepares the message cm848_j1939SendDiagnosticStatusMessage sends, which is PGN 65213 = FD1. Not a brake retarder.

plate_comment: Decodes the TSC1 requested torque byte (SPN 518, 1 percent per bit, offset -125 percent) into a retarding magnitude of 0 to 100 percent: 100 for raw values below 25, 125 minus the raw value up to raw 124, otherwise 0 (zero or positive torque). Called by cm848_processEngineRetarderTsc1Request with TSC1 byte 4; the result becomes engine_retarder_requested_torque_percent (was cm848_j1939SetupMultiFrameTransfer).
evidence: Code: raw < 0x19 -> 100, raw < 0x7d -> 0x7d - raw, else 0; both call sites pass tsc1_rx_byte_3 = data_pointer[3] = TSC1 byte 4 (SPN 518, j1939 DB). It sets up no multi-frame transfer.

plate_comment: Handles TSC1 (PGN 0) frames addressed to the engine retarder source address j1939_engine_retarder_source_address (routed by cm848_j1939DispatchAddressHandler); it ignores them when engine_retarder_configuration_mode is 0, for a data length other than 8 and for speed control requests (SPN 695 = 1), applies the per-sender request list and the override priority bits (byte 1 mask 0x30) and records the winning sender in engine_retarder_controlling_source_address / engine_retarder_controlling_source_index. For torque control (SPN 695 = 2) and torque limit control (3) it decodes the requested torque with cm848_decodeRetarderTorqueRequestPercent, quantizes it with cm848_selectEngineRetarderStagePercent and stores it as the torque request (engine_retarder_torque_request_percent) or the torque limit (engine_retarder_torque_limit_percent, 125 = none) that cm848_processGovernorErrorState arbitrates; override control mode 0 clears the request (was cm848_j1939ProcessGovernorRequest).
evidence: cm848_j1939DispatchAddressHandler routes TSC1 by destination: j1939_source_address -> torqueControlModeHandler (engine), j1939_source_address_b -> this function; j1939_source_address_b is 41 in the RAM dump = J1939 SA 41 Retarder, Exhaust, Engine #1, and ERC1 / RC are sent from the same SA. Speed control (SPN 695 = 1) returns at once, modes 2 / 3 call the decode + stage functions, and processGovernorErrorState reads the results (retarder request arbitration). The lead (TSC1 handler for the retarder source address) holds; the name says Tsc1 and engine retarder to match cm848_selectEngineRetarderStagePercent / cm848_calculateEngineRetarderTorque.

plate_comment: Builds and sends the ECM's RC broadcast (PGN 65249, Retarder Configuration, every 5000 ms on retarder queue 1, 19 data bytes so it goes out through the transport protocol) from the engine retarder source address: the first two bytes follow engine_retarder_configuration_mode (0xFF / 0x14 / 3) and engine_retarder_stage_1_weight, then five speed word + percent torque byte points (125 minus the percent) from the j1939_pgn65249_* / j1939_protocol_mode_* / DAT_0005c376 calibration words (was cm848_j1939BuildProtocolModeStatus).
evidence: Outside the lead list, found while tracing the ERC1 chain: header 0xFEE100 = PGN 65249 Retarder Configuration (j1939 DB: every 5 s and on change of the torque / speed points; the queue entry is (1, 0xfee1, 5000, ...), the retarder queue), data length 0x13 = 19 (> 8 so initiateJ1939TransportProtocol), source address j1939_source_address_b, torque bytes written as '}' (125) minus the percent high byte. The meaning of each payload byte was not verified.

plate_comment: Initialises the RC transmit descriptor (PGN 65249): CAN identifier from the priority word j1939_pgn65249_source_address_bits, 0xFEE1 and the engine retarder source address j1939_engine_retarder_source_address, data length 19 (0x13) and the payload pointers (start j1939_pgn_dest_address, end 0x3fae71) (was cm848_initJ1939ProtocolModeStatusBuffer).
evidence: Init partner of cm848_j1939BuildProtocolModeStatus (header 0xfee100 | priority << 26 | SA_b, length 0x13); see that row.

plate_comment: Sets the two interpolation cache words fuel_ema_mode_slot_state_1 / _2 (axis offset caches of the retarder torque lookup in cm848_calculateEngineRetarderTorque) to 2; called only by the ERC1 buffer init (was cm848_initSpeedControlTableDimensions).
evidence: xref: the only caller is cm848_initJ1939SpeedControlMessage; fuel_ema_mode_slot_state_1 is the first argument (cached_axis_offset) of the one lookupTableInterpolation in cm848_calculateEngineRetarderTorque, and _2 (0x3fa8a8) has 1 write and 0 reads. Nothing about speed control table dimensions.

plate_comment: Selects governor_tuning_set_blend_weight (0 = the governor_speed_error_*_working set, 128 = the _b set) from drivetrain_ratio through the six-entry tables at ROM 0x5a9c4 (ratio x 2048 breakpoints 1843 / 2458 / 3482 / 6144 / 10240 / 40960) and 0x5a9d2 (weights, all 128 in this ROM), or uses governor_tuning_set_default_blend_weight_cal when governor_system_config_flags mask 0x08 is set, then writes governor_speed_error_high / _low as the weighted blend of the two sets ((w x b + (128 - w) x working) >> 7). It runs only when its entry conditions hold (computed fuel demand below governor_speed_target_base plus a deadband, or the high idle override reset) (was cm848_calculateRpmLimitsFromProtection).
evidence: Code: loop index 1..6 compares drivetrain_ratio with the word at 0x5a9c4 + 2 * index and loads the weight at 0x5a9d2 + 2 * index; weight 0 / 128 copy the working / b pair, otherwise the 7-bit blend; nothing protection related. The ROM tables: axis words [12, 1843, 2458, 3482, 6144, 10240, 40960] and weights [12, 128 x 6].

ERC1 byte 1: 0xFF when the retarder broadcast flag is clear, else 0xC0 / 0xD0 (SPN 571 brake assist switch bits 5-6 = 00 / 01, SPN 572 = 11 not available) OR-ed with the SPN 900 retarder torque mode nibble; written only by the ERC1 builder and pointed to by the ERC1 descriptor.

The old comment (EEC2 engine percent load byte) is wrong: it is ERC1 byte 2 = SPN 520 actual retarder percent torque, written as 0x7d - (engine_retarder_torque_percent_times_256 >> 8) = 125 - percent, or 0xFF; EEC2 is PGN 61443 with its own builder.

Written once (word, value 2) by cm848_initJ1939SpeedControlMessage at +4 of the PGN 61440 descriptor 0x3fae10; the real PGN 65269 descriptor is at 0x3faab4 with its own j1939_pgn65269_tx_length at 0x3faab8. sendJ1939Message reads this field as the header data_length through the descriptor pointer only. Type stays word.
dword store of &j1939_vehicle_op_status_byte at +6 of the PGN 61440 descriptor (data_pointer field of j1939_tx_msg_t); mislabelled 65269. Type stays pointer / dword.
dword store of 0x3fae1e at +10 of the PGN 61440 descriptor (data_end_pointer field of j1939_tx_msg_t), the first byte after the 14-byte descriptor; mislabelled 65269. Type stays pointer / dword.
FD1 byte 1 = SPN 975 engine fan 1 estimated percent speed at 0.4 percent per bit: (j1939_diag_param_a x 5) >> 9; the old comment (scaled diagnostic parameter) hides what it is.

cm848_initJ1939BrakeRetarderBuffer uses (value & 7) << 2 as the top byte of the 29-bit CAN id, i.e. the 3-bit priority (same pattern as j1939_pgn61440_priority), not source address bits. Address 0x3fd87a is inside the EEPROM mirror (0x3fd482-0x3feec1), so the _cal suffix applies. Same issue for j1939_pgn61440_priority (0x3fd858) and j1939_pgn65269_priority (0x3fd83c): EEPROM-backed names without _cal.

Only reader is the FD1 builder: (value x 5) >> 9 becomes SPN 975 at 0.4 percent per bit, so 25600 = 100 percent (the unit is 1/256 percent, like engine_retarder_torque_percent_times_256). xref: 1 read, 0 writes in the whole binary, 0 in the RAM dump: the firmware never fills it (name states the consumer role; the old name says nothing).

Only reader is the FD1 builder: the first halfword, if below 16, becomes the SPN 977 fan drive state nibble (| 0xF0), else 0xFE; 0 writes anywhere, 0 in the RAM dump. Type note (do not change here): typed dword but only the first halfword is used (j1939_diag_code._0_2_ in the .cpp), word would be right.

Written only by cm848_processProtectionSystemBit4: j1939_engine_retarder_selection_percent (EBC1 SPN 973 input) or, when the J1939 input is off (fault_feature_config_flags bit 0 clear), 100 / 0 from switch_input_state_bits[1] mask 0x10, forced to 100 in governor_speed_limit_active_flag mode. Read by cm848_applyMinimumProtectionLimit (retarder percent limit) and by cm848_j1939BuildEngineControlByte, which sends it x 5 >> 1 = 0.4 percent per bit as EBC1 (PGN 61441) byte 5 = SPN 973 Engine Retarder Selection.

cm848_processProtectionSystemBit4 copies engine_retarder_selection_percent into it and zeroes it when engine_feature_enable_flags_cal mask 0x4000 is set and fault bits 32-47 mask 0x400 or 0x200 are set; its only reader is the ERC1 builder, which turns non-zero into SPN 571 brake assist enabled (0xD0 instead of 0xC0).

Set by cm848_processTemperatureCompensationMode from governor_mode_request_code (3 = operator selection from cm848_applyMinimumProtectionLimit, 2 = cruise from governorLoadMinimumUpdate, 4 = TSC1 torque limit from cm848_processGovernorErrorState) or fuel_correction_state (1 = TSC1 torque control); 0 = no request, 5 = init value. Only the ERC1 builder reads it (1 / 4 -> requester based mode, 2 -> cruise control, 3 -> operator selection).

cm848_processGovernorErrorState sets it to 0 (no TSC1 request) or copies j1939_source_address_index (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 = primary / secondary / tertiary / other TSC1 sender) when a TSC1 request wins; the ERC1 builder maps 1 -> mode 6, 2 -> 7, 3 -> 5, else 14. It is not a state machine.

cm848_processFuelEfficiencyTrim assigns it governor_speed_setpoint (the arbitrated retarder percent) or holds the old value while fuel_correction_trigger_flag is set; with governor_engage_mode_flags bit 0 set it sets logical output 11 (cm848_setLogicalOutputRequest(0xb, 0)) once the value has been 50 percent or more for governor_j1939_fuel_input_threshold_cal calls, and clears it below 50 percent. The ERC1 builder tests it for non-zero before reporting a torque mode. Not a fuel input. (governor_speed_setpoint 0x40a352 is the arbitrated request before the hold, same misnomer family.)

Set only by the retarder TSC1 handler (and cleared by init / reset): 0 = no request, 2 = torque control, 3 = torque limit control, the accepted SPN 695 value (speed control = 1 is rejected up front). Readers: cm848_selectEngineRetarderStagePercent (2 rounds up, 3 rounds down), cm848_processGovernorErrorState, governor_resetModeStateOnCondition, the history logger in phase_group_a_setupETC1Controller. Nothing speed governor related.

cm848_j1939ProcessGovernorRequest stores the TSC1 sender (msg->source_address) here and compares the next sender with it (same sender -> update, other sender -> priority arbitration); the history logger writes it as a source address byte (DAT_003feb6b).

cm848_lookupJ1939SourceAddressIndex(sender): 1 = j1939_tsc1_auth_primary_sa, 2 = secondary, 3 = tertiary, 4 = other, written only by the retarder TSC1 handler (and init / reset) and read by cm848_processGovernorErrorState, which copies it to engine_retarder_request_source_index. Rename only to say whose index it is.

Copy of engine_retarder_stage_percent in the TSC1 torque limit branch (mode 3), 125 (0x7d) in the torque control branch and at reset, 100 at init; cm848_processGovernorErrorState takes it as a limit when it is below governor_load_percent_min (the limit starts at 101). Not a transmitted value.

Copy of engine_retarder_stage_percent in the TSC1 torque control branch (mode 2); the only reader cm848_processGovernorErrorState passes it on as the retarder request when engine_retarder_override_control_mode is 2.

ROM calibration copied by cm848_copyROMCalibrationToRAM (1 write); 41 in the RAM dump = J1939 SA 41 Retarder, Exhaust, Engine #1. Its readers: the TSC1 destination match in cm848_j1939DispatchAddressHandler (routes to the retarder handler), the ERC1 and RC descriptor inits (source address byte), initiateJ1939TransportProtocol, cm848_dispatchJ1939ReceivedMessages, cm848_j1939_system_init (the ECM claims a second address for the retarder).

ROM word = 1 at the start of the retarder block (0x5c47c; the stage weights engine_retarder_stage_1_weight and the ramp words follow); its only readers are the retarder TSC1 handler (returns when 0), the ERC1 builder (byte 2 = 0xFF when 0) and the RC builder (byte 1 = 0xFF / 0x14 / 3 for 0 / 1 / above 1). 'dm' (diagnostic message) has nothing to do with it.

Units check: cm848_calculateEffectiveFuelLimit computes fuel = governor_fuel_demand_reference + (reference - speed) x 9813 / (8 x scale) with speed in 0.125 rpm and fuel in 0.0679 mm3 per stroke; 9813 x 0.06793478 x 0.0015 = 1.000, so scale counts are exactly 0.0015 rpm per mm3/stroke, the unit of e2m ASG_Droop_Axis / ASG_Alt_Droop_Axis (0.0015 RPM/MM3S). Written by cm848_calculateGovernorCompensatorCoefficients from the blend of two tables over speed_request_base (14333 at 740 rpm in the dump = 21.5 rpm per mm3/stroke), also used there to derive the PID gains. The lead holds.
cm848_calculateEffectiveFuelLimit refreshes it from governor_speed_scale_factor only while engine_operating_mode is 7 and uses the frozen copy otherwise; same quantity (droop) as its source.

Axis (speed_request_base, 0.125 rpm: 9000 / 12000 / 18000 / 21000 / 24000 / 27000 / 36000 = 1125 ... 4500 rpm) of one of the two droop tables blended by cm848_calculateGovernorCompensatorCoefficients; follows the all_speed_governor_droop rename.
Output (droop, 0.0015 rpm per mm3/stroke): 14333 / 13600 / 13533 / 19000 / 20267 / 20000 / 21000 (21.5 to 31.5 rpm per mm3/stroke); identical to the blend_128 values in this ROM.
Axis of the other blended droop table (same breakpoints as blend_0); weight governor_tuning_set_blend_weight = 128 in the dump selects this pair.
Output of the other blended droop table; values equal blend_0 values in this ROM.

Written only by cm848_calculateAllSpeedGovernorNoLoadFuel; it is the fuel offset of the droop line in cm848_calculateEffectiveFuelLimit (fuel = reference + error x 9813 / (8 x droop)) and the zero-error fuel the PID in cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor subtracts from fuel_demand_computed; dump value 183 = 12.4 mm3 per stroke at 740 rpm, a plausible friction (no-load) fuel.

cm848_calculateFuelTimingTarget sets speed_request_filtered = speed_request_base (no filtering) and cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor feeds it into exponentialMovingAverage, whose output is governor_reference_speed_filtered; so the variable is the filter INPUT, the opposite of its name. Also saved / restored by cm848_restoreEngineOperatingMode / cm848_engineMode_reset. Medium confidence on the exact replacement word.

Byte 1 of the logical_output_request_bits array at 0x40c080 (bit N = logical output N requested): 4 readers, 0 writers, byte width. Bits 3-7 (masks 0x08 to 0x80) are logical outputs 11-15, the engine retarder stage requests: cm848_calculateEngineRetarderTorque weighs them, cm848_processFuelEfficiencyTrim sets output 11 with cm848_setLogicalOutputRequest(0xb, 0), cm848_initProtectionEventStates clears outputs 11-15; the other readers (diagnosticMainStateProcessor, cm848_processTemperatureTrim, engine_protection_fuelCorrection_stateMachine) read the same bits. Alias row like logical_output_request_bits_16_to_31 (a struct-field / alias fix would be cleaner). Only stage 1 has weight 1 (ROM 0x5c47e..0x5c488 = 1,0,0,0,0,0), so this ECM has one retarder stage.

Only user is cm848_calculateChargingVoltageTarget: 0 selects the battery temperature table plus charging_voltage_target_offset, non-zero selects the fixed value (so 'enable' reads backwards; dump 0 -> table, charging_voltage_target 240). The wave-1 plate comment of the function already describes this. 0x4087f2 is not in the EEPROM mirror range, so _cal is dropped.

Only user is cm848_calculateChargingVoltageTarget: it becomes charging_voltage_target when charging_voltage_target_fixed_select is non-zero (dump 224). Renamed as the pair partner so the two names agree; _cal dropped (address outside 0x3fd482-0x3feec1).

Output of the slot 75 (0x4b) analog channel set up by cm848_sensorChannel7_init (0.5-4.5 V sensor: ADC 102 -> -6, ADC 921 -> 15988; the dump reads -2001 = ADC 0), not an engine speed (speeds are 0.125 rpm). Read by governor_speedFault_filterProcess_update, cm848_protection_init_2, cm848_calculateSensorDiagnosticValue, mpc555_processSensorValidation, cm848_processFaultTimingConditions. Neutral slot name like sensor_channel98_value; the physical sensor is not proven (its derived value feeds boost_pressure_filtered, so a boost-pressure type sensor is likely).

Default value (9216 in the dump) of the same slot 75 channel; its only reader boost_pressureSource_faultSelect_update uses it as boost_pressure_filtered while the channel is faulted. Neutral slot name like sensor_channel98_default_value.

governor_speedFault_filterProcess_update writes sensor value (slot 75) minus *psVar1, the filter reference DAT_003fbcc6 or the ROM word DAT_00406756 when DAT_003fd7f6 is non-zero; boost_pressureSource_faultSelect_update copies it to boost_pressure_filtered when the channel is fault free. The name states only the arithmetic; medium confidence on keeping 'reference' (the filter's reference value).

cm848_updateOilChangeMonitor ORs 4 (fault bits 80-95 mask 0x200) and 0x100 (fault bits 16-31 mask 0x2000) into the halfword at 0x3fee34 and clears it on the reset command; EEPROM mirror word (offset 0x19b2). Type note (do not change here): typed dword, but the code accesses a word at 0x3fee34 (the following halfword 0x3fee36 belongs to the fuel counter dword); the boot ROM time-shares it as a dword.

Alias row inside the old dword. disasm_func.py: dword loads / stores at 0x3fee36 in cm848_updateOilChangeMonitor: +1 per 557210 weighted injected-fuel units (0x8809a; 557210 x 0.06793478 mm3 = 37854 mm3 = 0.01 US gallon) and compared with the dword 250000 at DAT_00408a66 (2500 gallons); cleared by the reset command. EEPROM offset 0x19b4. Type note: this row should be a dword at 0x3fee36 (the +2 alias row has no type).

dword accesses in cm848_updateOilChangeMonitor: lifetime_distance_pulses - DAT_003fee42 (the lifetime distance at the last reset), compared with the dword 120000000 at DAT_00408a6a = 15000 miles at 8000 pulses per mile, and with the 16000000 (2000 miles) minimum at DAT_003fd8ec; cleared by the reset command. EEPROM offset 0x19b8. Type note: typed word, used as dword.

Not a fuel timing blend: its only read is the state term in the second difference equation of the PID loop in cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor, (acc + input x coeff[8] / 4 - previous output x coeff[10] / 4) >> 11, clamped into governor_demand_rate_limited, and its only write is the zero store in cm848_initFuelDemandVariables (xref: 1 read / 1 write); fuel_demand_pid_accum_hi / _lo (0x40a1cc / 0x40a1d4) show the same init-only pattern, so all three are filter accumulator terms that stay 0 here. Medium confidence on the exact word.

First argument (cached_axis_offset) of the lookupTableInterpolation call on engine_retarder_torque_stage_1_values in cm848_selectEngineRetarderStagePercent; initialised to 2 by cm848_initGovernorProtectionState; an interpolation search hint, nothing to do with diagnostics services.
Same as stage 1: cache word of the stage 2 table lookup in cm848_selectEngineRetarderStagePercent.
Same as stage 1: cache word of the stage 3 table lookup in cm848_selectEngineRetarderStagePercent.
Same as stage 1: cache word of the stage 4 table lookup in cm848_selectEngineRetarderStagePercent.
Same as stage 1: cache word of the stage 5 table lookup in cm848_selectEngineRetarderStagePercent.

Cache word of the single lookupTableInterpolation in cm848_calculateEngineRetarderTorque (it indexes whichever of the six stage tables is selected); reset to 2 by the ERC1 buffer init chain. Not an EMA mode slot.

Cache word passed with all_speed_governor_droop_blend_0_axis / _values (speed_request_base input) in cm848_calculateGovernorCompensatorCoefficients; the only other access is the init store of 2 in cm848_initLookupTableParams.
Cache word passed with all_speed_governor_droop_blend_128_axis / _values in cm848_calculateGovernorCompensatorCoefficients; only other access is the init store of 2.

ROM table read in cm848_blendGovernorTuningSets as the word at 0x5a9c4 + 2 * index for index 1..6 (xref_addr.py: word, 1 read, indexed lhzx): length word 12 then breakpoints 1843 / 2458 / 3482 / 6144 / 10240 / 40960 = drivetrain_ratio x 2048 (0.9 / 1.2 / 1.7 / 3.0 / 5.0 / 20.0).

ROM table loaded as the word at 0x5a9d2 + 2 * index in cm848_blendGovernorTuningSets (width word from the decompile; xref_addr.py finds no reference because the address is a literal base plus index): length word 12 then six weights, all 128 in this ROM (128 = the second tuning set only).

lifetime_distance_pulses captured at the oil change monitor reset command (the zero point of the distance since reset); read once and written once in cm848_updateOilChangeMonitor; xref_addr.py says dword (1 read / 1 write); inside the EEPROM mirror (offset 0x19c0).

cm848_updateOilChangeMonitor sets it to 1 when the distance, fuel or power accumulator exceeds its threshold and the minimum distance has passed, 0 otherwise and on reset; xref_addr.py says word (0 reads / 2 writes, the consumer reads it by another route).

Compared with the fuel counter at 0x3fee36 in cm848_updateOilChangeMonitor; value 250000 in the RAM dump = 2500 US gallons at 0.01 gallon per count; xref_addr.py says dword (1 read). Outside the EEPROM mirror, so no _cal.
Compared with the distance since reset (0x3fee3a); value 120000000 = 15000 miles at 8000 pulses per mile; xref_addr.py says dword (1 read).

Compared with oil_change_monitor_engine_power_accumulator_cal (0x3fee3e); value 89301300 in the RAM dump; xref_addr.py says dword (1 read). Named for the accumulator it limits, the soot reading was only by elimination.

Minimum distance since reset before the change-due flag can be set (the flag also needs one accumulator over its threshold); value 16000000 = 2000 miles at 8000 pulses per mile; xref_addr.py says dword (1 read); 0x3fd8ec is inside the EEPROM mirror (0x3fd482-0x3feec1), so _cal applies.
FD1 byte 2: fan_drive_state_code | 0xF0 (SPN 977 in the low nibble) or 0xFE; xref_addr.py says byte (0 reads / 1 write in cm848_j1939SendDiagnosticStatusMessage).

ERC1 / RC frame facts: the ERC1 descriptor has data length 2 (DLC 2, bytes 1-2 only) and the RC descriptor length 19 (transport protocol); both ride retarder queue 1, so they are sent only while datalink_broadcast_enable_flags bit 3 is set, and datalink_broadcast_enable_default_cal (EEPROM 0x3ee) is 0 in this truck's image, so neither is transmitted at power-up. j1939_pgn_dest_address (the first RC payload byte, 0xFF / 0x14 / 3 from engine_retarder_configuration_mode) and j1939_pgn65249_byte0 (second byte, from engine_retarder_stage_1_weight) are named as an address but are payload bytes (probably SPN 901 / 902 / 903 retarder type, location, control method); not renamed (field meaning unverified).

The channel is a 0.5-4.5 V input (ADC 102 -> -6, 921 -> 15988, default 9216) whose fault word 0x40be18 (sensor_channel75_fault_status) and fault-filtered value reach boost_pressure_filtered, but nothing ties it to a specific sensor (campaign: fault bits 642 / 643 have no usable DTC slot). governor_speedFault_filterProcess_update (0x506840), boost_pressureSource_faultSelect_update (0x506964) and governor_speedRamp_stabilityFlag_calc (0x507214) carry the same governor-speed vocabulary for this channel; suggest renaming the first to a sensor_channel75 name once the sensor is known.

fuel_trim_* family around cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor (not renamed, uncertain): in engine_operating_mode 7 fuel_trim_speed_active_flag is 1 when the two switch bits (switch_input_state_bits[1] mask 8 / [0] mask 4) are clear or fuel_trim_speed_switch_cancel_enable_flag is 0, vehicle_speed_copy >= fuel_trim_speed_minimum_vehicle_speed, no override and the park / neutral condition passes; then governor_reference_speed_filtered is pulled down (above fuel_trim_speed_upper_threshold it decays by fuel_trim_speed_decay_cal per call, else it is cut by fuel_trim_speed_lower_threshold), capped at current rpm + governor_reference_speed_lead_offset + manifold pressure gain and floored at governor_reference_speed_floor. That is a reference speed limiter of the speed governor, not a fuel trim; fuel_trim_pid_* / fuel_trim_saved_* are the saved / restored governor PID state of the same loop. A full rename pass needs the mode 7 owner (probably the road speed / PTO governor) identified first, so no names are proposed.
